name: Aqara SP-EUC01 (EU)

matter.note: No CSA listing found that names SP-EUC01. The plug is Zigbee; Aqara hubs with a Matter bridge (e.g. M3) can expose Aqara Zigbee devices to Matter.

apple_home.note: Aqara lists Apple HomeKit compatibility and states a hub is required.

google_home.note: Aqara lists Google Assistant compatibility and states a hub is required.

alexa.note: Aqara lists Amazon Alexa compatibility and states a hub is required.

smartthings.note: No official Aqara or SmartThings page found covering this plug.

home_assistant.note: Zigbee2MQTT supports it as SP-EUC01 and HA users run it via Zigbee, but no official HA or Aqara page found for this model.

hubRequired.note: Spec sheet: Hub Required: Yes. FAQ: it needs a hub and cannot connect to Wi-Fi directly.

localControl.note: Aqara FAQ: if the internet is down, app control stops but local control and links with other devices on the hub keep working.

energyMonitoring.note: Reports power and kWh consumption statistics in Aqara Home.

maxLoadWatts.note: 250 V AC, 10 A, max 2300 W. 16 A appliances are not supported.

summary: You'll need an Aqara hub before this plug does anything useful. The Aqara SP-EUC01 is a Zigbee 3.0 plug that can't join Wi-Fi by itself; once paired to an Aqara hub, Aqara lists it as working with Apple Home (HomeKit), Google Home and Alexa. It's rated 10 A / 2300 W and reports power and kWh in the Aqara Home app. If your internet drops, Aqara says local control and links with other devices on the hub keep working. Aqara's security update support for this model ended on 30 June 2026.
caveats: Needs an Aqara Zigbee hub; it cannot connect to Wi-Fi directly.
Rated 10 A / 2300 W, so it isn't meant for 16 A appliances.
Aqara's Product Security Support Policy lists the end of security updates for SP-EUC01 as 2026-06-30, a date that has already passed.
Home Assistant and SmartThings aren't officially documented for this model; Zigbee2MQTT supports it, but neither Aqara nor Home Assistant lists it.
